title: 🖥️ Apple May Cancel the OLED 'iMac' for Good — and Cost Is the Reason!
body: 🖥️ Apple May Cancel the OLED 'iMac' for Good — and Cost Is the Reason!

A new Korean report revealed that Apple is conducting a "comprehensive review" of its plans to launch an "iMac" with an OLED screen, and may delay the project or cancel it entirely. According to the report, Apple is in talks with "Samsung Display" about changing the development schedule for the "iMac" screen, after it was expected to launch with OLED in 2029 or 2030.

The biggest reason is cost: Apple uses tandem OLED technology, which uses two light-emitting layers, in the "iPad Pro" and "MacBook Pro", which raises manufacturing costs significantly, and rising memory prices make offering products at reasonable prices even harder. The second reason is weak sales: shipments of OLED "iPad Pro" screens fell 18% compared with last year, after the screen pushed up the device's price.

New CEO John Ternus, who took over in September, is also thought to be reassessing the commercial viability of expensive screens in more products. In a clear sign of a change of direction, Apple has asked its LCD screen suppliers, including "BOE", to develop screens for a new "iMac" expected to launch around 2029, meaning the "iMac" may keep an LCD screen for years to come. This comes after Apple launched this year its first "MacBook Pro" computers with touch-enabled OLED screens.

Simply put: an OLED screen is more beautiful and more expensive, but Apple sees that its price in a desktop computer that doesn't sell in large numbers may not be justified — a customer might prefer a lower price over deeper colors.
Does an OLED screen matter to you in a desktop computer, or is LCD enough for you?
